chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd, from Abī al-Jawzāʾ al-Munabbih ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his fathers, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, who said:
"The man is drawn out gently, and the woman is received from the front, and the person with the greatest right regarding the woman is at her rear."

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: The ghusl of a child is like the ghusl of an adult when he is deceased, like the rest of the dead. It is necessary that his ruling be their ruling regarding the obligation of ghusl for him, because he falls under the command.
And he said: The palm stalk is placed with all deceased Muslims—their elders and their young, their females and their males—as a sunnah (prophetic tradition) and a merit.

So the basis in it also is what we have mentioned: when they are commanded to place the palm stalk with the deceased, it is not restricted to an adult instead of a child, nor to a male instead of a female.
Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: The origin of placing the palm stalk with the deceased is that when Allah Most High sent down Ādam عليه السلام ... to the end of the hadith.

key_terms.الطِّفْلِ: the child, whose deceased-body ruling is discussed
key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةُ: the palm stalk placed with the deceased as a sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, in the context of funeral handling and burial procedure
key_terms.يُسَلُّ: is drawn out gently or extracted in the described funeral handling

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about washing a deceased child and placing the palm stalk with the dead?
ai.summary: This passage addresses legal rulings connected to the deceased, including handling the body, the ghusl of a deceased child, and the recommended placing of the palm stalk with Muslim dead. It emphasizes that these rulings apply generally, without distinction between adult and child or male and female.
